{{Short description|66th season of the National Hurling League}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox GAA League |league = 1997 National Hurling League |image = |dates = 9 March – 5 October 1997 |teams = 32 |team1 = Limerick |captain1 = |manager1 = |titles = 11th |team2 = |captain2 = |manager2 = |two= Dublin |four= |three = |previous = [[1995–96 National Hurling League|1995–96]] |next = [[1998 National Hurling League|1998]] }} The '''1997 National Hurling League''' (known as the '''[[Allianz|Church & General]] National Hurling League''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 66th season of the [[National Hurling League]]. ==Structural changes== At a meeting of Central Council on 18 May 1996, the [[Gaelic Athletic Association|GAA]] decided to scrap winter league hurling for a two-year trial period. It was also decided, by a margin of 23 votes to 15, to complete the National Hurling League within the calendar year. After further negotiations the GAA decided to run the league on a March to October basis. Other provisions included the playing of three matches in March, two in April and one each in May and June. The league final was to be played in October. Play-offs to determine the standings of teams within the divisions were also abandoned in favour of using scoring averages. ==Division 1== {{Infobox football league season |competition=[[National Hurling League|National Hurling League Division 1]] |season=1997 |winners=[[Limerick GAA|Limerick]]

[[Laois GAA|Laois]], [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] and [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] joined Division 1 as the promoted teams. On 5 October 1997, Limerick won the title after a 1-12 to 1-9 win over Galway in the final. It was their 11th league title overall and their first since [[1991-92 National Hurling League|1991-92]].{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|title=National Hurling League Results 1925-2009|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=18 April 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100805063526/http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|archive-date=2010-08-05|url-status=dead}} [[Clare GAA|Clare]], Laois and Wexford were relegated.
